title: 1978-10-10_SECTION_016_202.txt
concise_summary: PKD constructs an explicitly Gnostic theodicy in which YHWH and Christ are antithetical forces: the original creator maintains a tyrannical system of law, karma, and causality that imprisons consciousness, while Christ/Valis functions as a liberating invader who suspends causality itself through mercy and anamnesis. Drawing on John's Gospel, Spinoza, Buddhism, Gnostic cosmology, and his own 2-3-74 visions, PKD argues that immortality and true aliveness require short-circuiting the deterministic mechanical system—a daring inversion of traditional Christology.
key_claims: YHWH created and operates a deterministic, retributive system (Law, DNA, karmic causality) that makes humans 'not fully alive' and doomed to death; this is the Black Iron Prison or occlusion.
Christ/Valis is an 'invader' distinct from the original creator who sabotages this system through mercy, suspending causality and time itself to extricate souls from karmic machinery.

Gnostic dualism (not monism) correctly describes reality: Christ pits himself pragmatically against YHWH's elemental powers, proving them unjust by submitting a spotless victim to their retributive machinery.

Enlightenment (moksa) and Christian salvation are functionally identical: a waking-up from the Prison through anamnesis (remembering the pre-tyranny state) and accessing a divine intoxication/Kingdom 'not of this world.'
PKD's fiction (Ubik, Stigmata, Tears) depicts divine information and theophany—information-entities made of YHWH, Wisdom, Logos, and the divine Name—not alien invaders; his books are covert theology.
The Messenger dream reveals Christ's method: inserting a blank sheet between karmic bill of particulars and retributive processing, aborting 'the very machinery which is the basis of reality.'

tensions: PKD insists on antithetical dialectic (Christ vs. YHWH) yet fears that grounding reality in YHWH's Law is necessary to prevent non-being—tension between desire for liberation and fear of collapse.
The Kingdom is described as both real redemption and 'not real'/'magic'/'dream'/'fairyland'—PKD oscillates on whether Christ's realm has ontological weight or is intoxicated illusion.
He prefers the magical Kingdom but asks: 'If it's bipolarized to sein [being], do I still prefer it?'—unresolved uncertainty about whether enchantment compromises authenticity.
PKD acknowledges his theory means Gnostics were right to bifurcate Old and New Testaments, yet he calls YHWH 'the final bulwark against non-being'—cannot fully embrace Gnosticism.

Christ 'renders the Law void, hence the world irreal' to save us, yet PKD worries this means Christianity is 'anti-worldly' and involves 'split with the reality principle'—theodicy paradox unresolved.
His epistemological search leads to YHWH as Guarantor of reality, yet Christ saved him from the world—two incompatible allegiances.
Did PKD deliberately encode Tetragrammaton in Ubik (via 'I am'), or is it unconscious/prophetic? He admits uncertainty: 'I may have put word in deliberately, but I didn't know about the I am.'

uncertainty_flags: Reference to 'the talking horse's head' is unclear in context (possibly from PKD's dreams or a prior Exegesis entry not included here).

Title 'Faith of' is truncated—full work title unknown; could be 'Faith of Our Fathers,' 'Faith of a Few,' or unpublished fragment.
'Tears' is cited but never fully identified; possibly 'The Tears of Androids' or another work.
Reference to 'Rybus Rommey barfing up her guts' is cryptic—unclear if character, person, or symbolic image; not identified in text.
PKD mentions pentathol administration without full context—likely sedative used in 1974 but unclear if medical or experimental.
The 'three-fold' or 'binary' nature of divine nature (solar/lunar, masculine/feminine, Apollo/Dionysos) is explored but PKD never settles on a definitive cosmology.
Unclear whether PKD believes his 2-3-74 experiences were objective encounter, neurochemical event, or both simultaneously.

The Key for Freedom is to remember. Which is to say, remember how it was before the tyranny began : how it ought to be. One wakes up from the tyranny & occlusion (the talking horse's head).
